net sales.text: Total net revenues for 2024 were $61,562,000, an increase of $125,000, or 0.2%, compared to total net revenues of $61,437,000 for 2023 . See below for a further discussion of our sources of revenues for each of our pari-mutuel, Casino, food and beverage, and other revenues.

Casino.heading: CASINO REVENUES
Casino.text:
The primary source of Casino revenue is a percentage of the wagers received from the players as compensation for providing the Casino facility and services, referred to as “collection revenue.” Other revenue presented above includes fees collected for the administration of tournaments and amounts earned as reimbursement of the administrative costs of maintaining jackpot funds. Casino revenue represented 63.0% and 64.8% of the Company’s net revenues for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 , respectively.

Total Casino revenue decreased $1,006,000, or 2.5%, in 2024 compared to 2023 .The decrease can be primarily attributed to both a decrease in drop and a lower average collection revenue rate in table games, somewhat offset by an increase in our other table games revenue related to our progressive jackpot administration revenue.

Pari-mutuel.heading: PARI-MUTUEL REVENUES
Pari-mutuel.text:
Simulcast and Live Racing pari-mutuel revenues include commission and breakage revenues from on-track live and simulcast wagering. We receive guest fees from out-of-state racetracks and ADW companies for out-of-state wagering on our live races. Other revenues include source market fees paid by ADW companies for wagers made by Minnesota residents on out-of-state races and proceeds from unredeemed pari-mutuel tickets.

Total 2024 pari-mutuel revenue decreased $28,000, or 0.3%, compared to 2023 . The slight decrease in revenue in 2024 compared to 2023 is primarily due to a decrease in simulcast handle, somewhat offset by increased guest fees from out-state-handle on our live racing product on a per day basis due to increased field size and one additional live race day.

net sales.heading: REVENUES
net sales.text: Total net revenues for 2025 were $59,568,000, a decrease of $1,996,000, or 3.2%, compared to total net revenues of $61,562,000 for 2024 . For 2025 as compared to 2024 , total Casino revenue decreased 4.4%, pari-mutuel revenue decreased 6.6%, food and beverage revenue increased 3.5%, and other revenue decreased 0.7%. See below for a further discussion of our sources of revenues for each of our Casino, pari-mutuel, food and beverage, and other revenues.

Casino.heading: CASINO REVENUES
Casino.text:
The primary source of Casino revenue is a percentage of the wagers received from the players as compensation for providing the Casino facility and services, referred to as “collection revenue.” Other revenue presented above includes fees collected for the administration of tournaments and amounts earned as reimbursement of the administrative costs of maintaining jackpot funds. Casino revenue represented 62.3% and 63.0% of the Company’s net revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 , respectively.

Total Casino revenue decreased $1,688,000, or 4.4%, in 2025 compared to 2024 .The decrease was primarily driven by lower table games drop attributable to increased competition, as well as a lower average collection revenue rate resulting from a decreased hold percentage. These decreases were partially offset by an increase in our other table games revenue, driven by increases in our progressive jackpot administration revenue.

Pari-mutuel.heading: PARI-MUTUEL REVENUES
Pari-mutuel.text:
Simulcast and Live Racing pari-mutuel revenues include commission and breakage revenues from on-track live and simulcast wagering. We receive guest fees from out-of-state racetracks and ADW companies for out-of-state wagering on our live races. Other revenues include source market fees paid by ADW companies for wagers made by Minnesota residents on out-of-state races and proceeds from unredeemed pari-mutuel tickets.

Total 2025 pari-mutuel revenue decreased $540,000, or 6.6%, compared to 2024 . The decrease in pari-mutuel revenue in 2025 compared to 2024 is primarily due to a decrease in simulcast handle and decreased guest fees from out-state-handle on our live racing product due to decreases in field size and three fewer live race days.

Food and Beverage.heading: FOOD AND BEVERAGE REVENUES
Food and Beverage.text: Food and beverage revenues increased $277,000, or 3.5%, to $8,245,000 for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024 . The increase in food and beverage revenues is primarily due to increased catering operations and food revenues related to hosting large-scale special events.

Pari-mutuel.text:

The decrease in pari-mutuel revenue in 2025 compared to 2024 is primarily due to a decrease in simulcast handle and decreased guest fees from out-state-handle on our live racing product due to decreases in field size and three fewer live race days.

Food and Beverage.heading: FOOD AND BEVERAGE REVENUES
Food and Beverage.text: Food and beverage revenues increased $277,000, or 3.5%, to $8,245,000 for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024 . The increase in food and beverage revenues is primarily due to increased catering operations and food revenues related to hosting large-scale special events.

lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
